description: People judged the angle at which a paper tube would fall while a face looked at it. With open eyes facing the tube, the estimated angle was about $0.64^\circ$ steeper toward the face than away from it ($P = 0.006$, 147 online subjects), as if gaze pushed with about a hundredth of a newton. The effect vanished with a blindfold, a face turned away, a face said to look past the tube, or a tube said to be concrete, and no subject guessed the purpose.
limitations: The online sample gave no control of viewing distance. A low-level visual tilt illusion is not ruled out, and the effect is small.

sources.quote: This difference was statistically significant (two-tailed t test, t = 2.75, df 146, P = 0.006).
Other explanations of the data, for example involving a low-level visual tilt illusion, might still be possible.
